name: Red Flags When Choosing an ADU Additions Contractor in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What are early red flags that an ADU additions contractor in Los Angeles County might not be prepared for a complex addition project?
mainEntity.text: What are early red flags that an ADU additions contractor in Los Angeles County might not be prepared for a complex addition project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spotting warning signs early can save you from costly problems on an ADU addition. In Los Angeles County, a key red flag is a contractor who has built only detached ADUs or simple remodels and cannot show completed attached ADU additions similar to yours. Be cautious if they provide only a single lump‑sum price with no breakdown for design, permits, structural work, utilities, and finishes. Contractors who say permitting is “no big deal,” dismiss plan check corrections as rare, or claim they can skip engineered drawings for structural tie‑ins are not taking the complexities seriously. Another concern is vague or missing language about managing hidden conditions behind existing walls, roofs, or foundations; you want transparent contingency and change order processes. If a contractor pressures you to sign quickly, asks for a large upfront payment before design or permits begin, or hesitates to provide license and insurance details, treat these as serious warnings. Finally, pay attention to how they communicate: slow responses, incomplete answers, or visible frustration with your questions can foreshadow conflicts during the project. Choosing a contractor who is organized, transparent, and experienced with attached ADU additions greatly improves your odds of a smooth build.
acceptedAnswer.description: Red flags include a contractor who cannot show past attached ADU additions, gives only rough total prices without line items, downplays permitting complexity, avoids discussing hidden-condition contingencies, or refuses to work from engineered plans. These signs suggest limited experience with complex ADU additions.
